newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 2.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 2.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Friday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:

** Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said on Thursday that India can achieve a buoyant eight percent economic growth rate and expressed confidence there would be an increased inflow of foreign direct investment.

"I think India is on the march to take our rate of growth to eight percent from seven percent," Gujral said in an interview on the state-run Doordarshan television. "And I see no reason why we should not reach it," he said.

** Gujral however, warned that his government needed to take a bold decision to contain the oil pool deficit resulting from the gap between free market oil prices and the subsidised prices, fixed by the state, at which oil is sold by the refineries.
"That is unavoidable," he said in response to a question on the oil pool deficit. "It is an unfortunate part of government that sometimes bold decisions will have to be taken," he said.
"We will try to soften the blow as much as we can," Gujral said.
Analysts say pressure was mounting on the government to raise petroleum product prices to tackle the burgeoning oil pool deficit, estimated at 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) for 1996/97.
** Free-market reformer P. Chidambaram returned as India's finance minister on Thursday as Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral inducted six ministers into his 11-day-old centre-left government.

Chidambaram, considered an engine for economic reforms, was finance minister in the government of Gujral's predecessor, H.D. Deve Gowda, who stepped down after losing a vote of confidence on April 11.
MARKETS:
Indian stock markets will resume trading on Friday after a national holiday.
Bombay's benchmark 30-share index closed on Wednesday up 32.46, or 0.85 percent, at 3,841.11.
The National index rose 22.40 points to 1,079.85.
The Indian rupee opened steady at 35.75/76 against the dollar on Friday, dealers said. The rupee is seen testing the 35.75 barrier, they said.
STOCKS TO WATCH:
Indian Oil Corporation is raising a record $1 billion through a syndicated loan - a move that is bound to exert an upward pressure on the rupee, the Business Standard reports.
The $1 billion loan - the largest international fund rasing exercise by an Indian entity - amounts to one-fifths of the oil major's annual forex requirement of around $5 billion, the paper says.
** Koyoseiko, the $3 billion Japanese automotive major, has decided to increase equity in its Indian joint venture partner -Sona Steering by 12 percent, the Economic Times says.

The paper reports the Indian firm would issue 1.2 million shares in favour of the Japanese company at a rate of 92 rupees per share which is 22 rupees higher than the company's six month average quoted stock price.
The issue price is also 40 percent higher than its existing stock price of about 50 rupees in various stock exchanges.
** Ge Capital has hiked the intitial open offer for SRF Finance to 34.47 percent from 20 percent, the Business Standard says.
The paper says GE Capital has also roped in three other subsidiaries to act in concert, in picking up SRF Finance's public shareholding.
** Global Trust Bank and tyre major MRF Ltd are due to announce results for the year ending March 31, 1997 on Friday.
